confirmed.title: Non-atomic cancel can double refund/capture (no idempotency guard on the payment + status transition)
confirmed.detail: cancelBooking reads the booking, checks `booking.status !== "confirmed"` in app code (line 71), then calls the payments adapter `refund`/`capture` (lines 88-100), and only afterward sets status to `cancelled` (lines 102-105). The terminal UPDATE filters by `id` only and carries no `.eq("status", "confirmed")` precondition, and the mock adapter's capture/refund are non-idempotent blind updates (lib/integrations/payments/mock.ts:84-99). So two concurrent or retried invocations (two tabs, a Server-Action retry after a transient network/DB error, or a stale `pending` flag) both observe `status === "confirmed"`, both fire `capture`/`refund` for the same `payment_ref`, and the money operation runs twice. The CLAUDE.md money rule and the task explicitly require 'no double charge/refund'. The button's `disabled={pending}` in UpcomingBookings only guards one client instance, not concurrency. This is the one real money-correctness defect introduced by M12.
confirmed.suggestion: Make the cancel atomic and idempotent: perform the status transition as a guarded conditional UPDATE first — `update({status:'cancelled'}).eq('id',bookingId).eq('customer_id',profile.id).eq('status','confirmed').select()` — and only call payments.refund/capture if exactly one row was updated (i.e. this request is the one that won the transition). If zero rows change, return without touching payments. That guarantees the capture/refund runs at most once even under concurrent/retried calls.

confirmed.title: Receipt download links 404 for any booking without a completed session
confirmed.detail: The Receipts section renders a "Download receipt" link for EVERY payment row returned by listCustomerPayments (no status filter). But a confirmed/upcoming booking already has a payments row with status "authorized" (created by payments.authorizeHold in app/(customer)/actions.ts at booking time, before any session exists). The receipt route at app/(customer)/account/receipt/[bookingId]/route.ts does `const [booking, session] = await Promise.all([getBooking, getSessionByBooking]); if (!booking || ... || !session) return 404`. Since getSessionByBooking returns null until the session is completed, every authorized-but-not-yet-completed booking produces a visible receipt link that returns HTTP 404 when clicked. A customer who just booked an upcoming session will see a broken download.
confirmed.suggestion: Only render receipt links for payments tied to completed sessions (e.g. filter to status === "captured", or to bookings that have a completed session), or make the receipt route gracefully handle the no-session case (return a partial/authorized receipt instead of 404).

confirmed.title: Non-atomic check-then-act in cancelBooking allows a double refund/capture
confirmed.detail: cancelBooking reads the booking, verifies booking.status === "confirmed", then issues payments.refund()/capture() through the adapter, and only afterwards sets status to "cancelled". The final UPDATE is gated solely on .eq("id", bookingId) with NO status precondition. Two concurrent cancelBooking calls (or a cancel racing the session-start flow) both pass the in-memory status check, so both invoke a payment mutation against booking.payment_ref for booking.price_block_cents before either flips the row to cancelled. With a real payments provider this is a double refund or double capture of customer money — a money-integrity gap on a financial path. Note rescheduleBooking in the same file already guards its write with .eq("status", "confirmed"); cancelBooking is missing the equivalent guard.
confirmed.suggestion: Make the state transition the gate for the side effect: perform the status flip first as a conditional, atomic UPDATE — supabase.from("bookings").update({ status: "cancelled" }).eq("id", bookingId).eq("customer_id", profile.id).eq("status", "confirmed").select() — and only call payments.refund()/capture() when that update returns exactly one row (i.e. this call won the transition). This ensures the refund/capture runs at most once per booking.

confirmed.location: const next = upcoming[0]; (Resume card uses next for `account.nextSession`)
confirmed.title: "Next session" shows most-recently-created booking, not the soonest-scheduled one
confirmed.detail: `upcoming` is derived directly from listCustomerBookings, which orders by created_at DESC (lib/db/queries.ts listCustomerBookings). `next = upcoming[0]` is therefore the most recently CREATED confirmed/in_progress booking, not the chronologically next session. With two upcoming bookings — e.g. one scheduled next week (booked today) and one scheduled tomorrow (booked yesterday) — the Resume card labeled "Next session" will show next week's booking. The Upcoming bookings list is likewise displayed in created_at order rather than by scheduled time.
confirmed.suggestion: Sort upcoming by scheduled_at ascending (treating talk-now/in_progress as soonest) before picking next and before rendering the list, so "Next session" and the list order reflect actual chronology.

confirmed.location: Receipts list <a> (lines 183-189) and components/customer/PastSessionsTable.tsx actions column (lines ~44-66)
confirmed.title: Repeated receipt/rate links share identical accessible names with no per-item context
confirmed.detail: Every payment row renders an anchor whose entire accessible name is "Download receipt" (t("account.download")), and every past-session row renders "Rate" and "Receipt" links. With more than one row the link list a screen-reader user pulls up is "Download receipt, Download receipt, ..." / "Rate, Receipt, Rate, Receipt, ..." — indistinguishable, so the user cannot tell which booking/listener/date each refers to (WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose). axe does not flag duplicate link text, so the existing axe test (single-row) passes despite the problem. The table gives visual row context but the links themselves carry none programmatically.
confirmed.suggestion: Give each link a distinguishing accessible name, e.g. an aria-label built from the row data: `Download receipt for {listenerName}, {dateLabel}` and `Rate your session with {listenerName} on {dateLabel}`. Keep the short visible text but append the context via aria-label or a visually-hidden span.

confirmed.title: Payment status rendered as raw machine enum, unlocalized and read verbatim
confirmed.detail: The badge prints p.status directly, so the payment_status enum values "authorized" / "captured" / "refunded" / "failed" (lib/supabase/database.types.ts:634) are shown as-is and spoken verbatim by a screen reader. This is a raw token rather than human-readable copy and violates CLAUDE.md rule 7 (all user-facing strings via messages/en.json) — every other status in the diff (bookings, availability) goes through a localized label map. Additionally a "failed" payment renders with tone="neutral" (grey), so a failure is not visually distinguished from a normal non-captured state; meaning rests on the lowercase token text alone.
confirmed.suggestion: Add a status->message map (e.g. account.payStatusCaptured / Authorized / Refunded / Failed) and render the localized label. Map "failed" to tone="alert" so the visual treatment matches the meaning and isn't carried by text alone.

confirmed.title: Reschedule success announces a meaningless label fragment to screen readers
confirmed.detail: After a successful reschedule the live region announces t("account.nextSession") which resolves to the bare string "Next session" (messages/en.json:362) — a UI label, not a confirmation of what just happened. The reschedule panel also closes (setRescheduleId(null)) and the inputs clear with no visible/announced success state, so a screen-reader user gets no meaningful feedback that the reschedule succeeded. Compare the cancel path on the same component (lines 35-38) which correctly announces a dedicated confirmation message. This is a live-region/feedback gap introduced by this diff.
confirmed.suggestion: Add a dedicated message (e.g. account.rescheduled = "Booking moved to your new time.") to messages/en.json and announce that instead of t("account.nextSession"). Consider surfacing it via toast(..., "success") for parity with the name-save flow, and move focus back to the booking's action area after the panel closes.

confirmed.title: Hardcoded "min" suffix bypasses messages/en.json
confirmed.detail: The minutes label is rendered as a hardcoded `{item.blockMinutes} min` string in JSX. This violates CLAUDE.md rule 7 (all user-facing copy through messages/en.json) and is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase, which renders minutes via i18n everywhere else: `t("provider.minutesShort", { minutes })` (SessionsTable, IncomingRequests, provider dashboard), `t("summary.minutesValue", { minutes })` (session summary), and `t("receipt.minutes", { minutes })` (the receipt route in this same diff). The literal " min" will not localize.
confirmed.suggestion: Reuse an existing minutes message key (e.g. the diff already added `receipt.minutes` = "{minutes} min"), or add an `account.minutesShort` key, and render `t("...", { minutes: item.blockMinutes })` instead of the bare ` min` literal.

confirmed.title: cancelBooking does not Zod-validate bookingId at the boundary
confirmed.detail: Per CLAUDE.md rule 5 every server action must validate input with Zod at the boundary. cancelBooking accepts a raw string and passes it straight into supabase .eq("id", bookingId) / the later UPDATE with no uuid validation, unlike addFavorite (validates uuid) and rescheduleBooking (rescheduleSchema). Ownership is still enforced by the customer_id check and RLS, so this is not an IDOR, but it is an inconsistent boundary-validation gap; a malformed id also produces a Postgres 'invalid input syntax for type uuid' error thrown from the query rather than a clean 'Booking not found.'.
confirmed.suggestion: Validate bookingId with the existing `uuid` schema at the top of cancelBooking (e.g. `if (!uuid.safeParse(bookingId).success) return { ok: false, error: "Booking not found." };`) before any query, mirroring addFavorite/rescheduleBooking.

confirmed.title: Inconsistent boundary validation of ids vs sibling actions
confirmed.detail: Sibling actions in this same file validate their id inputs with Zod before touching the DB — `addFavorite` runs `uuid.safeParse(providerId)` and `rescheduleBooking` uses `rescheduleSchema` (bookingId: uuid). But `cancelBooking` passes `bookingId` straight into `.eq("id", bookingId)` with no uuid check, and `removeFavorite` passes `providerId` straight into `.eq("provider_id", providerId)` with no uuid check. Both still check role + ownership (cancelBooking compares customer_id; removeFavorite scopes by customer_id), so this is defense-in-depth/consistency rather than a hole, but it's the kind of boundary-validation gap CLAUDE.md rule 5 calls out and reads as an inconsistency next to the validated siblings.
confirmed.suggestion: Add `if (!uuid.safeParse(bookingId).success) return { ok: false, error: "Booking not found." };` at the top of cancelBooking, and the same `uuid.safeParse(providerId)` guard already used in addFavorite to removeFavorite, so all four actions validate ids uniformly.

confirmed.location: upcoming list filter (line ~77-78) + components/customer/UpcomingBookings.tsx cancel button (lines 84-100)
confirmed.title: In-progress bookings render a Cancel button that always fails
confirmed.detail: The account page builds `upcoming` from bookings with status `confirmed` OR `in_progress` and passes them to UpcomingBookings. UpcomingItem carries no status, so UpcomingBookings renders a Cancel button for every item including in-progress sessions. cancelBooking guards `status !== 'confirmed'` and returns `{ok:false, error:'This booking can't be cancelled.'}`, so an in-progress cancel just surfaces an error toast. No money is mis-handled (the server guard correctly refuses), but offering a Cancel/Reschedule action that can never succeed for an active session is a UX defect on the M12 dashboard.
confirmed.suggestion: Pass the booking status (or an `isActive` flag) through UpcomingItem and hide Cancel/Reschedule for `in_progress` items (show only Join), or filter in-progress bookings out of the cancel-eligible list.

confirmed.title: Receipt route does not validate bookingId is a UUID before querying
confirmed.detail: The route passes the raw path param bookingId into getBooking/getSessionByBooking with no Zod/uuid validation at the boundary (CLAUDE.md rule 5). getBooking does `if (error) throw error`, so a malformed bookingId (non-uuid) triggers a Postgres 'invalid input syntax for type uuid' error that propagates as an unhandled 500 instead of the intended 404 ('receipt.notFound'). Ownership itself is correctly enforced here (RLS read plus the explicit booking.customer_id !== user.id check), so this is robustness/validation, not a data leak.
confirmed.suggestion: Validate the param with z.string().uuid().safeParse(bookingId) right after reading ctx.params and return the 404 'receipt.notFound' response when it fails, before calling getBooking/getSessionByBooking.

confirmed.location: Settings Card rows, lines ~32-64 (Email / Payment method / Notifications / Language)
confirmed.title: Label/value setting rows use unassociated spans instead of a description list
confirmed.detail: Each settings row is two sibling <span>s — a bold label (Email, Payment method, Language) and a value — with no programmatic association between them. A screen reader reads them as adjacent inline text with no name/value relationship, and the pairing isn't conveyed semantically. These are textbook definition pairs that should be marked up as such.
confirmed.suggestion: Wrap the rows in a <dl> with <dt> for each label and <dd> for each value (the StatusBadge can live inside the <dd>). This conveys the label/value relationship to assistive tech without changing the visual layout.

confirmed.location: cancel(id) onClick of the Cancel button
confirmed.title: Cancel button cancels irreversibly on a single click with no confirmation
confirmed.detail: Clicking "Cancel" calls cancelBooking immediately. The action can charge the full block per the cancellation policy (cancellationOutcome → capture) when a scheduled session is within 1h of start, so an accidental single click can both cancel the booking and charge the customer. A confirmation string `account.cancelConfirm` ("Cancel this booking?") was added to messages/en.json for exactly this but is never used.
confirmed.suggestion: Gate the cancel action behind a confirmation (use the existing account.cancelConfirm string via a Dialog/confirm step) before invoking cancelBooking.

confirmed.location: cancel button onClick={() => cancel(item.id)} (lines ~76-83); unused message account.cancelConfirm
confirmed.title: Destructive cancel executes on a single press with no confirmation step
confirmed.detail: The Cancel button immediately calls cancelBooking, which can capture/charge the customer's block when cancelled inside the policy window (actions.ts cancelBooking -> payments.capture). The diff even adds an account.cancelConfirm = "Cancel this booking?" message (messages/en.json) but nothing references it (grep finds zero usages). For a blind/low-vision user an accidental activation triggers an irreversible, money-moving action with no guard. This is a safety/usability gap rather than a strict WCAG failure.
confirmed.suggestion: Gate the cancel behind a confirmation using the existing Dialog primitive (or at minimum a two-step inline confirm) wired to the already-present account.cancelConfirm string, mirroring how other destructive flows confirm before acting.

confirmed.location: cancel(), lines 32-44 and the Cancel button at lines 1097-1104
confirmed.title: Cancel fires immediately with no confirmation, leaving cancelConfirm orphaned
confirmed.detail: The Cancel button calls `cancel(item.id)` directly on click, which immediately invokes the `cancelBooking` server action (a destructive action that can capture/charge the full block per the cancellation policy). There is no confirmation step, even though the diff added `account.cancelConfirm` ("Cancel this booking?") to the catalog — that key is never used (see dead-keys finding), strongly implying a confirm dialog was intended but dropped. Reschedule got an inline confirm UI; cancel did not.
confirmed.suggestion: Either wire `account.cancelConfirm` into a confirmation (the codebase already has components/ui/Dialog for this), or, if instant-cancel is intentional, delete the orphaned cancelConfirm key. Pick one so the catalog and behavior agree.

confirmed.title: Three dead message keys added but never referenced
confirmed.detail: This diff adds `account.removeFavorite` ("Remove {name} from favorites"), `account.cancelConfirm` ("Cancel this booking?"), and `account.settingsHeading` ("Payment & settings") to the catalog, but grep across app/ and components/ shows zero usages of any of them. `account.removeFavorite` is also a duplicate of `favorite.remove` ("Remove {name} from favorites"), which is the key actually used by FavoriteButton. `account.settingsHeading` duplicates the used `account.settingsTitle`. `account.cancelConfirm` was evidently authored for a cancel confirmation that was never wired up (see related finding).
confirmed.suggestion: Remove the three unused keys. FavoriteButton already uses `favorite.remove`, and the settings pages use `account.settingsTitle`/`settingsLink`, so nothing else needs to change.
